applicationInfo.name: Kinesis Cross-Account KPL/KCL Sample
applicationInfo.description: Cross-account streaming pipeline using KPL (AssumeRole) and KCL (resource-based policy) across three AWS accounts

assumptions.content: All communication uses TLS (enforced by AWS SDKs)
EC2 instances in default VPC with security groups restricting inbound access
IMDSv2 enforced (HttpTokens: required) preventing SSRF credential theft
KMS key rotation is enabled (automatic annual rotation)
External ID is a shared secret; production should use unique per-customer values
Deployer IAM permissions are appropriate; sample does not manage deployer IAM
EC2 instances are ephemeral demo resources; production should use ASGs

threats.title: Confused deputy attack on cross-account role
threats.description: A malicious service tricks Account B into granting stream write access to an unauthorized principal by abusing the cross-account AssumeRole trust

threats.title: EC2 instance metadata theft via SSRF
threats.description: Attacker exploits application vulnerability to steal instance profile credentials from the EC2 metadata service

threats.title: Stream data tampering via over-privileged producer role
threats.description: If producer role has broader permissions than PutRecords, a compromised instance could modify stream configuration or delete the stream

threats.title: DynamoDB lease table poisoning
threats.description: Attacker with write access to KCL lease tables could manipulate shard assignments or roll back checkpoints causing data reprocessing

threats.title: Unattributed cross-account writes
threats.description: Without CloudTrail, writes from Account A via assumed role cannot be traced to the originating principal

threats.title: KMS key policy overly broad
threats.description: Key policy grants to account root; any principal in the producer/consumer account can potentially encrypt/decrypt stream data

threats.title: Stream data exposure via broad resource policy
threats.description: Resource policy grants read access to the entire consumer account root rather than a specific IAM role

threats.title: Internal infrastructure details in git history
threats.description: Internal GitLab URLs in commit history could reveal internal tooling if repo is published without history rewrite

threats.title: Shard exhaustion by rogue producer
threats.description: Compromised producer writes at maximum rate exhausting shard capacity and starving legitimate consumers

threats.title: DynamoDB throttling on lease tables
threats.description: High lease-churn scenarios could throttle KCL metadata operations causing consumer stalls

threats.title: Producer role escalation to stream write access
threats.description: If EC2 instance is compromised, attacker inherits sts:AssumeRole permission and gains cross-account stream write access

threats.title: Wildcard resource on CloudWatch and STS actions
threats.description: cloudwatch:PutMetricData and sts:GetCallerIdentity use Resource: * which cannot be scoped to specific resources

mitigations.content: External ID condition on AssumeRole trust policy prevents confused deputy attacks
IMDSv2 enforced via HttpTokens: required; blocks SSRF-based credential theft
Least-privilege producer role: only PutRecord, PutRecords, DescribeStream, DescribeStreamSummary, ListShards on specific stream ARN
DynamoDB IAM scoped to specific named tables; no wildcard table access
CloudTrail enabled by default; AssumeRole and Kinesis API calls logged with source identity
KMS key policy grants only GenerateDataKey*/Decrypt to producer, only Decrypt to consumer; not kms:*
Accepted for sample; documented that production should scope resource policies to specific IAM roles
Documented requirement to squash/rewrite git history before pushing to public GitHub
KPL rate limiting (150%) + Kinesis provisioned capacity (2 shards = 2 MB/s hard limit)
DynamoDB on-demand mode auto-scales to handle burst lease operations
KPLProducerRole can only AssumeRole on one specific cross-account role ARN; assumed role scoped to stream-only actions
AWS service limitation; cannot scope further. Documented with cfn_nag suppression justification.
